issues.description: Close control message uses wrong type string per Deepgram Speak API
issues.detail: The PR description and linked Deepgram references describe a control message of {"type": "CloseStream"} (the STT/Listen convention), but the code sends {"type": "Close"}. The Speak v1 socket client uses CloseStream for graceful termination. If the server does not recognize "Close", the WebSocket will be torn down without the very acknowledgment this PR claims to wait for, defeating the fix and reintroducing the 429/lingering-session symptom. State the invariant explicitly: 'after _close_ws returns, the server has acknowledged a CloseStream and no further audio will be billed.' That invariant does not hold as written.

issues.description: Single receive() with 1s timeout is not a correct termination proof
issues.detail: The loop here is implicit: we send Flush, send Close, then await exactly one frame. There is no stated invariant about what that one frame is. It could be a binary audio chunk still in flight from before the Flush, a metadata frame, or the close acknowledgment. Treating any-frame-received as 'cleanly closed' is asymptotically OK but practically wrong: in the common case the awaited frame is leftover audio and the actual close ack arrives after the 1.0s timeout, which then silently swallows the TimeoutError. Either drain until a typed Close-ack frame is seen (bounded by a deadline) or document precisely why a single frame suffices.

issues.description: Bare Exception catch in close path obscures categories of failure
issues.detail: `except Exception as e` covers ConnectionResetError, CancelledError-adjacent conditions, and programmer errors (e.g. ws already closed) identically, then logs at warning. For a close path this is defensible, but the literate version distinguishes 'ws already closed by peer' (expected, debug-level) from 'send_str failed for unexpected reason' (warning). As written, every benign close races will log a warning, which trains operators to ignore the channel.

issues.description: Comment claims a guarantee the code does not provide
issues.detail: The comment says the wait prevents race conditions and 429 errors 'from lingering sessions.' That is the goal, not the proof. With a 1-second timeout that silently passes on expiry, the code provides at-best-effort, not a guarantee. A literate comment should state the invariant honestly: 'best-effort drain up to 1s; on timeout we proceed with close and accept the residual 429 risk.' Otherwise the next reader will assume the race is closed when it is merely narrowed.

issues.description: Constants are class attributes but accessed via the class name from a method on the same class
issues.detail: `SynthesizeStream._FLUSH_MSG` is referenced inside `_close_ws`, which is a method on the enclosing class (the chunked stream). This works only because both classes happen to be in scope; the FLUSH/CLOSE constants logically belong to whichever object owns the protocol framing. Either move them to module scope (they are protocol constants, not instance state) or reference them via `self.__class__` only when actually on SynthesizeStream. As written, a careful reader has to verify that the class reference is not a copy-paste from elsewhere.

review.summary: Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED, leaning NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The change moves in the right direction — sending a control message before close is the documented Deepgram convention — but the audit does not survive scrutiny. The most load-bearing issue is that the PR description and linked references specify {\"type\": \"CloseStream\"} while the code sends {\"type\": \"Close\"}; if the server requires the former, the acknowledgment-wait this PR adds is waiting for a message that will never come. The single-frame receive with a swallowed 1.0s TimeoutError is a best-effort drain dressed up as a termination proof; the comment should say so plainly. Fix the message string (or verify against the live Speak v1 protocol and document why \"Close\" is correct), state the invariant the close sequence actually establishes, and the change is good to land.
